name: Light Light Green
lede: Light Light Green is a pale, almost washed-out mint from the 2010 xkcd color survey, named by doubling the modifier *light* on the plain word *green* rather than borrowing a new word.

sections.title: A doubled modifier
sections.body: Repeating a modifier, as in *light light green*, is the survey's way of pushing further along a scale than the single word *light* already does; the library files it as a direct child of [[green]] [1][2]. A near-duplicate xkcd entry, Washed Out Green, sits about 2.2 units away, close enough that the two likely describe the same impression to different volunteers [2]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system's closest block, very light yellowish green, is 5.3 units off [2]. The nearest named colors on file are [[very-light-green]], [[celery]] and [[very-light-green]], at 2.6, 3.1 and 4.2 ΔE [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries a color within four units of Light Light Green covering at least one per cent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. A green this pale and this saturated at once is an unusual combination for aged oil paint, which tends to either fade toward grey or darken with varnish rather than stay this bright and light together [3]. In printed English the phrase rose fastest and peaked in the 1930s, though it stays rare overall [4].

questions.q: Why is the name "Light Light Green" written with "light" twice?
choices: To push further along the lightness scale than "light green" alone
It names two different greens mixed together
It refers to a two-tone paint
questions.answer: To push further along the lightness scale than "light green" alone

openers: Light Light Green doubles its own modifier just to go paler still.
